requirements.quote:
The exporter value is computed as:

   TLS-Exporter(label, context_value, key_length) =
       HKDF-Expand-Label(Derive-Secret(Secret, label, ""),
                         "exporter", Hash(context_value), key_length)
requirements.condition: when computing a TLS exporter value
requirements.required_behavior: compute TLS-Exporter(label, context_value, key_length) as HKDF-Expand-Label(Derive-Secret(Secret, label, ""), "exporter", Hash(context_value), key_length)
requirements.why_checkable: Exporter test vectors can verify the nested derivation, labels, context hash, empty Derive-Secret transcript, and output length.

requirements.quote:
Where Secret is either the early_exporter_master_secret or the
   exporter_master_secret.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use a secret outside the two specified exporter master secrets
requirements.why_checkable: The secret supplied to the exporter derivation can be traced to one of the two key-schedule values.

requirements.quote:
Implementations MUST use the
   exporter_master_secret unless explicitly specified by the
   application.
requirements.condition: when an application has not explicitly selected the early exporter
requirements.why_checkable: The default exporter API path can be tested to identify which key-schedule secret it uses.

requirements.quote:
A separate
   interface for the early exporter is RECOMMENDED; this avoids the
   exporter user accidentally using an early exporter when a regular one
   is desired or vice versa.
requirements.condition: when an implementation exposes both regular and early exporters
requirements.required_behavior: provide a separate interface for the early exporter
requirements.why_checkable: The public exporter API can be inspected for distinct regular and early-exporter entry points.

requirements.quote: If no context is provided, the context_value is zero length.
requirements.condition: when the exporter caller provides no context
requirements.why_checkable: A context-omitted exporter call can be instrumented or compared with an explicit zero-length context call.

requirements.quote:
Consequently, providing no context computes the same value as
   providing an empty context.
requirements.condition: when exporter inputs differ only between an absent context and an empty context
requirements.forbidden_behavior: distinguish absent and empty contexts in exporter output
requirements.why_checkable: Two exporter calls with otherwise identical inputs can be compared byte-for-byte.

requirements.quote:
Future
   specifications MUST NOT define a use of exporters that permit both an
   empty context and no context with the same label.
requirements.condition: when a future specification defines an exporter use
requirements.forbidden_behavior: permit both an empty context and no context under the same exporter label
requirements.why_checkable: This constrains future specification authors rather than a TLS implementation.

requirements.quote:
New uses of
   exporters SHOULD provide a context in all exporter computations,
   though the value could be empty.
requirements.condition: when defining a new use of TLS exporters
requirements.required_behavior: specify a context for every exporter computation, allowing that context to be empty
requirements.why_checkable: This is specification-design guidance and does not constrain behavior of an implementation of this RFC.

requirements.quote:
Requirements for the format of exporter labels are defined in
   Section 4 of [RFC5705].
requirements.required_behavior: follow the exporter-label format requirements in Section 4 of RFC 5705
requirements.why_checkable: The quoted evidence only points to external requirements and does not state the format needed for a self-contained implementation check.

requirements.quote:
The first class of attack can be prevented by sharing state to
   guarantee that the 0-RTT data is accepted at most once.  Servers
   SHOULD provide that level of replay safety by implementing one of the
   methods described in this section or by equivalent means.
requirements.required_behavior: provide replay safety that causes a given 0-RTT data flight to be accepted at most once across the server system
requirements.why_checkable: Repeated delivery of the same 0-RTT flight across the deployment can measure whether more than one acceptance occurs.

requirements.quote:
Therefore, in normal
   operation, clients will not know which, if any, of these mechanisms
   servers actually implement and hence MUST only send early data which
   they deem safe to be replayed.
requirements.condition: when a client sends early data without knowing the server's replay protection
requirements.required_behavior: send only early data that the client deems safe to replay
requirements.forbidden_behavior: send replay-unsafe data as early data
requirements.why_checkable: The client's early-data eligibility policy and call sites can be inspected and tested against replay-safety classification.

requirements.quote:
The server MUST ensure that any
   instance of it (be it a machine, a thread, or any other entity within
   the relevant serving infrastructure) would accept 0-RTT for the same
   0-RTT handshake at most once;
requirements.condition: when the same 0-RTT handshake is replayed to one server instance
requirements.required_behavior: allow that server instance to accept 0-RTT for the handshake at most once
requirements.forbidden_behavior: allow one server instance to accept 0-RTT more than once for the same handshake
requirements.why_checkable: A repeated ClientHello and early-data flight can be sent to the same instance and acceptance counted.

requirements.quote:
The "at most once per
   server instance" guarantee is a minimum requirement; servers SHOULD
   limit 0-RTT replays further when feasible.
requirements.condition: when stronger replay limitation is feasible
requirements.required_behavior: limit 0-RTT replay acceptance beyond the per-server-instance minimum
requirements.why_checkable: Deployment-level replay tests can count acceptances across instances and compare them with the minimum bound.

requirements.quote:
The second class of attack cannot be prevented at the TLS layer and
   MUST be dealt with by any application.
requirements.condition: when an application uses TLS 0-RTT and client retries can duplicate an application message
requirements.required_behavior: deal with retry-induced replay at the application layer
requirements.why_checkable: The phrase "dealt with" does not identify a concrete required defense, invariant, or rejection behavior.

requirements.quote:
Note that any application
   whose clients implement any kind of retry behavior already needs to
   implement some sort of anti-replay defense.
requirements.condition: when an application's clients implement retry behavior
requirements.why_checkable: The text requires only "some sort" of defense and gives no checkable minimum behavior in this evidence.
